terms.label: Inductance
terms.plain: Inductance tells how current stores magnetic energy.
terms.meaning: A scalar coil coefficient or symmetric inductance matrix, according to the attached contract.
cautions: Drawing diameter and turns are not a measured inductance.

terms.label: Resistance and useful load
terms.plain: Resistance converts electrical energy to heat.
terms.meaning: The receiving load and winding/internal losses are accounted for separately.
cautions: R1 can also name a research round; ℝ denotes real numbers, not resistance.

terms.label: Electrical current
terms.plain: Current is the flow rate of electric charge.
terms.meaning: Lowercase i(t) is instantaneous; uppercase I is a phasor whose peak/RMS convention must be declared.
cautions: The imaginary unit i in an impedance equation is a different meaning.

terms.label: Voltage and source-port drive
terms.plain: Voltage is electrical potential difference between two points.
terms.meaning: Instantaneous voltages and complex source-port phasors are distinct representations.
cautions: A source knob is not automatically a measured port voltage; declare peak or RMS.

terms.label: Real average power
terms.plain: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred.
terms.meaning: Real average source power uses the real part of voltage times conjugate current, with a convention-dependent factor.
cautions: Peak phasors need a factor ½; RMS phasors do not.

terms.label: Stored energy
terms.plain: Energy can remain in the capacitor and magnetic field.
terms.meaning: Initial and final stored states belong in a finite-time source-work budget.
cautions: Released initial energy is not unexplained energy production.

terms.label: Work transferred over time
terms.plain: Work is energy transferred during a chosen interval.
terms.meaning: Integrating signed instantaneous power gives work; uppercase W here is a variable, while W after a number is the watt unit.
cautions: Lowercase w in the witness contract denotes a voltage, not work.

terms.label: Calibration and deterministic error bounds
terms.plain: Calibration connects instrument readings with a stated reference.
terms.meaning: These contracts supply deterministic error radii in volts, amperes, henries or dimensionless transfer units, as declared.
cautions: A stipulated error radius is not measured sensor performance or a confidence interval.

terms.label: Not to scale
terms.plain: A sketch may show relationships without preserving size ratios.
terms.meaning: Use written dimensions and declared coordinate units rather than measuring screen pixels.
cautions: An accurate-looking diagram is not an engineering drawing or a calibrated photograph.

terms.label: Estimate, difference and time derivative
terms.plain: Marks over a symbol tell you which version, change or bound is meant.
terms.meaning: A hat denotes an estimate; δ often a difference or perturbation; Δ can denote a final-minus-initial change or a supplied error bound, according to the contract; a dot is a time derivative.
cautions: Δa and ΔM in these contracts are error-bound radii, not temporal changes. Every symbol needs declared units; ż is velocity, not position.

terms.label: Contact and magnetic force
terms.plain: A magnet can change how strongly an object presses on a balance.
terms.meaning: N is upward contact force; Fm is the stipulated upward magnetic force and mg the downward weight.
cautions: A smaller contact reading does not establish changed gravity; N the variable differs from N the unit.

terms.label: Mass and gravitational acceleration
terms.plain: Mass and gravitational acceleration together determine weight.
terms.meaning: In the static comparison g is stipulated as 9.80665 m/s², not inferred from a balance change.
cautions: m as mass differs from m as the metre unit.

terms.label: Position, velocity and inductance gradient
terms.plain: Changing position can change the modeled inductance.
terms.meaning: z is prescribed position, ż its time derivative and dL/dz the stipulated inductance change per metre.
cautions: This z is not impedance Z; prescribed motion is not a solved free trajectory.

terms.label: SI and unit prefixes
terms.plain: SI is the international system of measurement units.
terms.meaning: cm=0.01 m, mm=0.001 m, µ=10⁻⁶, milli=10⁻³ and nano=10⁻⁹ of the stated unit.
cautions: A source drawing in cm or mm is not silently a metres-based parts table.

equations.title: Motion and storage both draw on source work
equations.equation: vI = RI² + d(½LI²)/dt + Fż; F = ½I² dL/dz
equations.plain: The source supplies heat, stored field change and mechanical work.
equations.convention: Maintained current; stipulated L(z); externally prescribed motion, not free dynamics.
equations.units: Every power term W; F N, ż m/s, dL/dz H/m.
cautions: The chosen inductance law and motion are not measured hardware.

signalSteps: The source maintains the stipulated current while the modeled inductance changes with position.
